digest.component_or_area: code-review criterion dispatch and project criteria routing
propositions: New hard-fail CI gates/floors/caps broke pre-existing in-flight branches (medium-loved-newt, impudent-sodium-ferret, rancid-aerophobic-skylark, brattish-ladyish-jaguar) because code-review gate has no criterion checking whether a branch predating a pipeline/gate change would now fail.

Project code-review criteria are today injected unconditionally regardless of changed files, so applies_to globs have no effect on project criteria—the approved portable design is unimplementable without a seam fix.

The criterion must be triggered via declarative applies_to globs covering eight CI vendors (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab, CircleCI, Azure Pipelines, Buildkite, Bitbucket, Drone) rather than hard-coded CI-specific file paths, and the glob set must be project-overridable via [code_review] ci_config_globs config key.

Implementation requires two core behavioural changes: filtering activated project criteria by their applies_to globs against changed files in gate_dispatch._activated_code_review_project_criteria, and validating applies_to_config_key pointers in overlay loading.

Gerrit change 1919 exceeds authorized scope—the approved design is project-owned (.rebar/ content only), but the change adds ~145 lines of core behaviour change and a new shipped public config key, altering dispatch semantics for all project code-review criteria.

Operator decision rejected the criterion on grounds that new gates breaking in-flight branches should be fixed by rebase-and-correct, not institutionalized via compatibility mechanisms; ticket closed unimplemented with no code landing.
